packageOwnership.$comment: The organism-boundary ownership map (ADR-0074, amended by ADR-0075), read by packages/cli/src/check-boundaries.ts (`pnpm check:boundaries`, wired into `pnpm gate` + the CI verify job). Every @storytree/* package under packages/* is classified EXACTLY once as an `organism` (owned by one story). The gate asserts every real runtime cross-organism dependency edge (each package.json `dependencies`; devDeps are test scaffolding and excluded, ADR-0010 §5) is COVERED by a declared cross-story edge — consumer-side in the consumer story's `depends_on`, OR provider-side in the provider story's `consumed_by` (stories/*/story.md, ADR-0074 §4) — so cross-organism coupling can't be added without a declared edge, and because the studio forest renders `depends_on`, every coupling is therefore UI-visible. NOTE (ADR-0075, 2026-06-19; the ports renamed for role-not-position per ADR-0078, 2026-06-20): the shared ports storage-protocol/proof-protocol are NO LONGER an exempt `substrate` class — they are ordinary ROOT organisms (stories/storage-protocol + stories/proof-protocol, depends_on [] / [proof-protocol]) that every consumer DECLARES depends_on, exactly like cli/store stopped being exempt 'composition roots' in ADR-0074 §2. They stay listed in `foundational` (a SUBSET of organisms, not a class) to carry ONE minimality rule the gate enforces — a foundational port may only depend on another foundational port — which keeps them zod-only / node+pg-free so the studio's browser bundle works. So a port dependency is a visible declared+rendered edge, not an invisible exemption.
packageOwnership.$comment_surfaces: Consuming SURFACES (ADR-0100): a surface name → the story that owns it. A surface is an apps/* app (the studio) — a sink that wires organisms together and is consumed by nothing. ADR-0100 brought apps/* into the same boundary scan as packages/*: a surface's package.json @storytree/* deps are COVERED by the same rule as an organism's (declared in the surface's own story depends_on), so the studio's real wiring is enforced + rendered, exactly the visibility-over-exemption call ADR-0074 §2 made for the cli/store hubs. A surface is never `foundational` and draws no inbound edge. (The public-website subrepo is also a consuming surface but ships no workspace package — its forest-world edge is a declared story node backed by the check:web-engine drift gate, ADR-0093, not a package scanned here.)

sourceOwnership.$comment: The SECOND declared ownership map (ADR-0317 D2), at SUBTREE grain — the `packageOwnership` pattern one level down, read by packages/cli/src/ownership.ts (`storytree ownership`). `packageOwnership` above answers 'which story owns this PACKAGE' and check:boundaries holds it to the disk at 24/24. Nothing answered 'which addressable unit is responsible for this FILE', and the natural candidate cannot: `proof.real.sourceFile` is typed `sourceFile: string`, a total function unit→the one file that unit AUTHORS, so it inverts into ownership neither surjectively (its image is bounded by the 296-node count, not the 519 files) nor injectively (apps/studio/src/components/TreeView.tsx is named by SEVEN units). That field is NOT decayed — 111 owned against 117 declared-and-existing targets, ~95% full — it simply was never an ownership map, and `scope.sourceGlobs` is a per-phase WRITE FENCE deliberately broader than what a unit owns (which is why check-boundaries.ts:227 filters globs out of the proof-bound set). NEITHER field is read here and neither changes: the prove-it-gate, the phase machine, the write scopes and every signed verdict carry ZERO risk from this map. GLOBS ARE PERMITTED HERE and refused there, because this map binds no verdict. VALUE = an addressable object in the work graph: a CAPABILITY id by preference (the grain claims are taken at, ADR-0270 D1), or a story id where no capability is the honest answer; ADR-0317 D3 makes a declared subtree itself claimable. REPORT-ONLY: `storytree ownership` renders this and fails nothing, and a BLOCKING rung must earn its place on this report's own numbers first (ADR-0311 retired sixteen rungs for want of evidence). ### AUTHORED IN FULL 2026-08-06 (first-class-edges-arc), 527 of 527 files owned, and three authoring rules the next editor must keep. (1) MIXED GRAIN, WITH THE SPLIT REPORTED. Capability grain wherever a capability's stated outcome names or plainly covers the subtree's job; story grain only where the tree HAS no such capability. Measured on landing: 363 files (68.9%) capability-grain, 164 (31.1%) story-grain. Story grain is legal (ADR-0317 D3) but it satisfies totality while leaving 'claim the capability you are writing' nothing finer to bind to — which is the arc's founding measurement, now COUNTED instead of assumed. The residual concentrates in four places and IS the story-author worklist: `cli` 51 (gate rungs, drains, generated-view builders, doctors), `studio` 34, `drive-machinery` 13, `desktop` 11. Two of the story-grain owners are NOT gaps — `proof-protocol` (8) and `storage-protocol` (6) are root-port stories that carry no capabilities because the story IS the one competence. NO BLANKET BUCKET: every owner here names a real object in the work graph (`storytree ownership` resolves all 372 and reports 0 unresolved); an invented 'substrate' owner would drive the number down while changing nothing. (2) DECLARATIONS ARE DISJOINT — never a specific entry plus a broader one covering it. The judge collects EVERY match and reports a second one as CONTESTED regardless of key order, so the ordering-based 'specific before broad' pattern would light that warning permanently over 350+ files — every file sitting under a specific entry — and destroy the signal. Order is therefore free here and contested==0 means what it says. Use `<dir>/*.ts` for a non-recursive directory (`*` never crosses `/`) when a subdirectory needs a different owner; a bare `<dir>` claims everything beneath it and is right only where the whole tree is one competence (packages/forest-world/src, packages/procedural-architecture/src/buildings). (3) THE ENTRY COUNT IS 372, NOT 'tens'. ADR-0317 expected subtree grain to keep entries in the tens; measured, the economy holds where directories are homogeneous (24 packageOwnership entries; forest-world in one line) and breaks in FLAT, HETEROGENEOUS src/ directories where ownership genuinely varies file by file — packages/cli/src is 100 files fronting ~20 different organisms. 372:527 is what totality actually costs here. A new file lands UNOWNED and must be declared; that is the totality check working, and it is why no catch-all is left to swallow it silently.

baseline.$comment: The measurement `storytree ownership` prints its trend against — the evidence base a future blocking rung would have to argue from. Re-record it deliberately, not on every edit: a moved baseline erases the trend it exists to show.

subtrees.$section_cli: packages/cli — the verb surface. Most modules here FRONT another organism's competence, so the honest owner is that organism's capability, not the `cli` story: `drift.ts` is binding-staleness's, `tree.ts` is notice-board's, `deploy-health.ts` is studio-cloud's. What is left over — the gate rungs, drains, projections and doctors — has no capability anywhere in the tree, and is declared at story grain so the report counts it.
subtrees.$section_cli_residual: STORY GRAIN, and each one is a capability the tree does not have. These are the gate rungs, drains, generated-view builders and doctors — real competences with no addressable unit finer than the `cli` story to claim. Counted as story-grain by `storytree ownership`; see the block $comment.
subtrees.$section_drive: packages/drive — the shared build/orchestrate drivers (ADR-0112). Nearly every module is a named drive-machinery capability or the driver half of another story's capability; the residue is composition glue.
subtrees.$section_orchestrator: packages/orchestrator — the deterministic spine and the proof ruler. The best-mapped package in the repo: drive-machinery decomposed the spine capability-by-capability, so almost every file has a real owner one grain below the story.
subtrees.$section_agent: packages/agent — the leaf executors behind the PhaseAuthor seam.
subtrees.$section_library: packages/library — the knowledge tier. `src/store` is the seam (seed entry); the root barrel splits by competence between the library story's own capabilities and the UAT/proof-binding stories that host their pure computes here.
subtrees.$section_ports_and_boards: The two root ports and the two small board/member organisms. Each is one competence end to end, so a directory-grain entry IS the honest grain here rather than a shortcut.
subtrees.$section_studio_server: apps/studio/server — the shared API route table. Owned largely by studio-cloud, library-review and studio-members capabilities rather than by the `studio` surface story.
subtrees.$section_studio_components: apps/studio/src/components — the renderer. The Library lens components map one-to-one onto library-tech-tree-overlay capabilities; the forest map does not. TreeView.tsx is declared at STORY grain deliberately: SEVEN units name it, so no single capability is responsible for it, and that is the ADR-0317 non-injectivity finding standing in one file.
subtrees.$section_studio_shell: apps/studio — the SPA shell, the Playwright/Vitest configs and the story-UAT spec.
subtrees.$section_desktop: apps/desktop — the thick client. The backend routes are desktop capabilities one-to-one; the Electron shell, keychain and credential ports are the two credential/shell capabilities; `src/apply` (the ADR-0117 brokered rebuild loop) has no capability yet.
subtrees.$section_world_and_art: The render core, the shared app surface, the R3F website engine and the art factory.
subtrees.$section_uat_organisms: The UAT-witness organisms — the best-decomposed corner of the tree, where nearly every file is its own capability.
subtrees.$section_traversal: The four context-traversal organisms — every non-barrel file is a named capability.

hostedStories.$comment: ADR-0192 decision 2 — the packages-forward GRANDFATHER register: the FROZEN list of stories whose unit proof-bound sources (proof.real.sourceFile + literal sourceGlobs) already lived inside ANOTHER story's building (a foreign packages/<x> or apps/<x> dir) at adoption (2026-07-13), derived mechanically via the landlord rule's evidence (rule 5, PR #720). check-boundaries.ts passes this register's keys to the pure judge (packages/cli/src/boundaries.ts): a hosted story ABSENT from the register is REFUSED regardless of declared edges (a NEW story's code lives in its OWN workspace package — packages-forward), and a register entry with NO hosting evidence is a STALE violation (remove it) — so the register is the self-pruning migration worklist (ADR-0192 decision 3: migrate one story at a time, whole footprint at once). Entries only ever LEAVE as stories migrate; ADDING one is a loud, owner-reviewed diff. Every entry below already carries a declared host edge (the increment-1 remediation), so the landlord rule is green over them.
